title: Shimeji Mushroom Larb with Lime and Toasted Rice
changes_from_base: Blanched shimeji mushrooms replace the minced beef, so there is no frying; the dressing stays sour-led with fish sauce, lime and toasted rice.
summary: A fast, sour and herby Thai-style larb of quickly blanched shimeji mushrooms with shallots, fish sauce, lime, chilli and nutty toasted rice powder.
equipment: pestle and mortar or spice grinder

ingredients.item: fish sauce (check the label: fish, salt and sugar only)
dried chilli flakes or Thai chilli powder
little gem lettuce, leaves separated, to serve

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Toast the rice in the dry pan over medium heat, shaking, 6-8 min until deep golden. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.

steps.title: Blanch the mushrooms
steps.text: Bring a pan of water to the boil. Dip the mushrooms in a sieve in batches for 15 sec, shake off the water and tip into the bowl.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Toss in the shallots, 1 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tbsp lime, then taste: it should be mainly sour. Add the rest of the fish sauce, lime and chilli as needed.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Toss through the rice powder, culantro and mint and serve straight away with lettuce leaves.

tips: Blanch the mushrooms only 15 seconds so they stay firm.
Make extra toasted rice powder; it keeps for weeks in a jar.
Coriander and mint stand in well if you cannot find culantro.
storage: Best eaten straight away; the mushrooms release liquid as it stands. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
